你说：
what it means? ImPlot::PlotShaded("Stock 3", xs1, ys3, 101, shade_mode == 0 ? -INFINITY : shade_mode == 1 ? INFINITY : fill_ref, flags);
ChatGPT 说：

That line is a C++ call to ImPlot that draws a shaded area plot, with the shading reference changing depending on shade_mode.

Let’s break it down piece by piece 👇

The full line

cpp
ImPlot::PlotShaded(
    "Stock 3",
    xs1,
    ys3,
    101,
    shade_mode == 0 ? -INFINITY :
    shade_mode == 1 ?  INFINITY :
                       fill_ref,
    flags
);

What ImPlot::PlotShaded does

PlotShaded draws a filled (shaded) region between:

  • a curve (xs1, ys3)

  • and a reference value (baseline)

Typical uses:

  • fill under a curve

  • fill above a curve

  • fill between a curve and a constant value

Meaning of each argument

ArgumentMeaning
"Stock 3"Label of the plot
xs1Array of x-values
ys3Array of y-values
101Number of points
fill_ref (computed)Baseline to shade to
flagsPlot configuration flags

The important part: the ternary expression

cpp
shade_mode == 0 ? -INFINITY :
shade_mode == 1 ?  INFINITY :
                   fill_ref

This is a nested ternary operator, equivalent to:

cpp
double baseline;

if (shade_mode == 0)
    baseline = -INFINITY;
else if (shade_mode == 1)
    baseline = INFINITY;
else
    baseline = fill_ref;

What each shade_mode means visually

shade_mode == 0

cpp
baseline = -INFINITY;

✅ Shade downward to the bottom of the plot
(“fill under the curve”)

shade_mode == 1

cpp
baseline = INFINITY;

✅ Shade upward to the top of the plot
(“fill above the curve”)

Any other value

cpp
baseline = fill_ref;

✅ Shade between the curve and a custom reference value
(e.g., y = 0, average price, threshold, etc.)

In simple terms

“Plot a shaded area for ‘Stock 3’.
If shade_mode is:

  • 0: fill downward

  • 1: fill upward

  • otherwise: fill to fill_ref”
